I created `docs/policies/password-hashing.md`. It records argon2id as the current password hashing decision, made on 2026-09-25. It gives the recorded rationale: argon2id is memory-hard, which defends against GPU attacks, and its design resists side-channel attacks.

The only source is a single memory observation (#1, "Adopting argon2id for password hashing"). The repo has no ADR or policy files, and a search for hashing terms found nothing in the code. The other recorded decisions (serialization, license, versioning, TLS verification, HTTP) don't touch password hashing, so nothing revokes or replaces observation #1. I left out any alternative algorithms.

I haven't committed the file.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. I didn't need them for this task.
